comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Verified against the pinned herdr 0.8.0 rather than reasoned about.

A daemon started with the config Muster now writes - `[update]` holding only `version_check = false` - fetches `2026.08.29.1` into its state dir. Its `osc_title_working` regex covers `\x{25D0}-\x{25D3}` as well as Braille, and it adds the `live_turn_working` screen rule.

`herdr agent explain --file <screen> --agent claude --json` on a screen showing a turn in progress:

    with the fetched manifest:   version 2026.08.29.1 | state working | rule live_turn_working
    with only the bundled one:   version 2026.07.13.1 | state idle    | rule none

That command is worth knowing about on its own: it needs no daemon, and it reports `manifest_source`, `manifest_version` and the matched rule. It is how the option set below was settled.

**Two of the card's four options are not available.** herdr reads override manifests from `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/herdr/agent-detection/`, not from the directory `HERDR_CONFIG_PATH` names - measured: a manifest placed beside Muster's derived config is ignored and detection falls back to `bundled`. So "pin manifests with Muster" and "place overrides" are one mechanism, and both mean writing into the user's own herdr config directory, which `configuration.md` promises Muster leaves alone.

Nobody's dot says `working` yet: a running daemon keeps the manifests it loaded, so a machine picks the new set up when its daemon next restarts. The card's per-machine workaround still applies until then.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
A pane whose agent is visibly working - Claude Code mid-turn, spinner in its title, tokens counting up - carries the grey idle dot in the agent list. Noticed on a devenv pane; the whole point of the list is that the dot answers "what is this agent doing" without reading the pane.

**Muster is rendering the daemon faithfully.** Asked at the moment the screenshot was taken, herdr's own snapshot for that pane said:

    agent: "claude"          agent_status: "idle"
    terminal_title: "◑ Claude Code"     (the spinner is Claude Code's working marker)
    revision: 645            state_change_seq: 3

The agent was identified, the pane had been revised 645 times, and the agent state had moved three times in the life of the session. So the wrong answer is the daemon's, and the fix - or the report - is upstream. What belongs to Muster is that a dot which is confidently wrong is worse than one that admits it does not know: `unknown` and `idle` are drawn differently, and the daemon said `idle`.

## What every transition today looked like

Eleven `agent.state` records across both machines, a full day of real use with agents running on each:

    unknown -> idle      x5
    idle    -> unknown   x2
    idle    -> blocked   x2
    blocked -> idle      x2

    local:  idle x4, blocked x2
    devenv: idle x3, unknown x2

**`working` never appears - not once, on either machine.** herdr's `AgentStatus` has five values (`idle`, `working`, `blocked`, `done`, `unknown`, per `docs/observations/herdr-0.8.0.md`), and one of the five is doing nothing. The state machine is otherwise alive: `blocked` was detected twice on the laptop, which is the transition that matters most and works.

The second pattern in the same table - `blocked` only ever on local panes - has a duller explanation than the tunnel: that devenv session was running with bypass permissions on, so it never asked for anything. Nothing to block on, nothing to detect. **This is not an ssh problem.**

## Reproducing it

1. Run an interactive Claude Code in a muster pane, local or remote, and give it a task that takes a minute.
2. While it is visibly working, ask the daemon directly:

       HERDR=/Applications/Muster.app/Contents/Library/MusterSessions.app/Contents/MacOS/herdr
       HERDR_SOCKET_PATH=<that daemon's socket> $HERDR api snapshot   # look at agents[]

   and compare with the dot in the sidebar and with `muster window`.
3. Read the whole day's transitions out of the run logs, which is where the missing state shows up:

       rg '"event":"agent.state"' ~/Library/Logs/muster/*.jsonl

**A trap:** `claude -p "..."` is not a reproduction, and its result is not evidence either way. Print mode reported `idle` for its whole run on the local daemon - measured - but nothing says it should report otherwise: it draws no interactive UI, sets no spinner, and a detector keying on what the screen shows has nothing to see. Whether a headless agent ought to register at all is a separate question from this card. Use an interactive session.

## Validating a fix

- A pane with an agent mid-turn reports `working`, and the dot differs from the one it carries at rest.
- The full set of transitions over a working session includes `working` at all - the log line above is the cheapest check, and today it would have failed.
- `blocked` keeps working on the laptop, and starts appearing on remote panes too.
- If it turns out to be herdr's, the Muster-side question is still worth answering: should a status the daemon reports confidently but wrongly be drawn as confidently? A dot that says `idle` about a working agent costs more than one that says nothing.

## Root cause: a stale detection manifest that Muster forbids updating

herdr detects an agent's state from rules in a per-agent manifest (`src/detect/manifests/claude.toml` in herdr's tree). Exactly one rule in the claude manifest can produce `working`:

    [[rules]]
    id = "osc_title_working"
    state = "working"
    priority = 1100
    region = "osc_title"
    regex = ['^[\x{2800}-\x{28FF}] ']

`U+2800–U+28FF` is the Braille block - the `⠋⠙⠹` spinner Claude Code used to draw in its terminal title. The title on the pane in question was `◑ Claude Code`, and `◑` is `U+25D1`, in Geometric Shapes. The regex cannot match, so **`working` is unreachable for current Claude Code**, on any machine.

The rest of the state machine survives because it does not go through the title. `idle` comes from `live_prompt_box`, which looks for the `❯` prompt box on screen; `blocked` comes from the permission-prompt rules, which look for "do you want to proceed?" and friends. Both are screen rules, both still fire - which is exactly why the dot looks alive while being unable to ever say "working".

**Upstream has already fixed it.** The manifest published at `https://herdr.dev/agent-detection/claude.toml` is version `2026.08.29.1` - two days before this was found - and reads:

    # Braille covers <= 2.1.227; half-circles are the 2.1.228 busy spinner.
    regex = ['^[\x{2800}-\x{28FF}\x{25D0}-\x{25D3}] ']

It also adds a `live_turn_working` screen rule, so working no longer depends on the title alone. herdr 0.8.0 bundles `2026.07.13.1`.

**And Muster is what stops the fix arriving.** Every daemon Muster starts is handed `~/.muster/state/herdr.toml`, which Muster rewrites on every launch:

    [update]
    version_check = false
    manifest_check = false

herdr's manifest precedence is bundled, then a fetched copy in its state dir, then a local override in `<config>/agent-detection/<agent>.toml`. With `manifest_check = false` the middle one never happens, so a Muster-run daemon is frozen on whatever manifests its pinned binary shipped with - for as long as that pin stands.

## The decision worth revisiting

`version_check = false` is well argued in `docs/configuration.md`: a daemon that could fetch a different version of itself would make "this was tested against the daemon it ships with" mean nothing. That reasoning is about the binary.

Manifests are not the binary. They are data describing how a third-party agent looks on screen, and those agents change on their own schedule - Claude Code changed a spinner glyph and took the feature Muster is built around with it. Freezing them buys reproducibility in a place where the outside world moves weekly, and the cost is silent: nothing says the rules have gone stale, the dot just stops being able to say one of the things it knows how to say.

Four ways out, none of them free:

- **Pin manifests the way herdr is pinned.** Ship a manifest set with Muster, checksummed, updated when the pin is. Keeps reproducibility, moves detection onto Muster's release cadence, and adds a thing to remember at release time.
- **Let manifest updates through.** One line, and the daemon tracks upstream - at the cost of detection rules changing under a build that was tested against different ones.
- **Place overrides.** Muster already writes files onto a remote machine; it could write `<config>/agent-detection/*.toml` too. Same staleness problem, moved.
- **Expose the choice.** A `manifest_check` knob in `~/.muster/config.toml` puts it in the user's hands, which is the honest answer if there is no good default.

## Workaround, per machine

Place the published manifest where an override wins, then restart that daemon - manifests are cached in-process, so a running daemon keeps what it loaded:

    curl -fsSL https://herdr.dev/agent-detection/claude.toml \
      -o ~/.config/herdr/agent-detection/claude.toml

On a devenv the same file goes at `<remote home>/.config/herdr/agent-detection/claude.toml`, and the daemon there has to be restarted the `setsid` way described in `a_2HvxMgXai` - leave it running before relaunching Muster, or the attach hits `a_2HpkpQlZP`.
title: 💤 The dot says idle while the agent is working
